[P3] Lucas paradox
In economics , the Lucas paradox or the Lucas puzzle is the observation that capital does not flow from developed countries to developing countries despite the fact that developing countries have lower levels of capital per worker . Poor countries have lower levels of capital per worker -- which explains , in part , why they are poor . In response , savers in rich countries should look at poor countries as profitable places in which to invest . In reality , things do not seem to work that way . Surprisingly little capital flows from rich countries to poor countries .
